deltaUnderReview.netEconomicVerdict: The delta changes NO issuance quantity, NO pricing input, and NO cap accounting. Per unit of antimatter the protocol still emits `amount` unbacked phUSD plus `calculateMintAmount(stable, amount_rescaled)` backed phUSD, exactly as at 0bb82d8. All five wont-fix economic Mediums are economically NEUTRAL under the delta (details in deltaAssessments). The delta adds one new external liveness dependency and one new atomic revert surface, both Low and both conditional on an owner registration choice.

deltaAssessments.basis: The unbacked half is `_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount)` at Antimatter.sol:260, identical in effect to 0bb82d8. Neither the pre-quote nor the equality check nor the caller-only change touches this line's operand: it is still the raw 18-decimal antimatter quantity, independent of exchangeRate, decimals, cap and quote. Requiring the caller to own both halves does not alter aggregate issuance per unit of antimatter — it only changes WHO must hold the stable leg. Owner rationale (antimatter was generated from prior staked stablecoin) is unaffected in either direction.

The exact-equality check CANNOT interact with the daily cap, because the cap is a revert, never a haircut: PhusdStableMinter.sol:221 `require(config.mintedToday + phUSDAmount <= config.maxMintPerDay, 'Daily mint limit exceeded')` and 222 `config.mintedToday += phUSDAmount`. A cap over-run aborts inside minter.mint at Antimatter.sol:251 and the equality check at 257 is never reached, so a cap event can never surface as a PhUSDAmountMismatch. Independently confirmed that the pre-quote cannot encode a cap: calculateMintAmount (minter:243-256) reads only config.exchangeRate and config.decimals and never maxMintPerDay / mintedToday / lastMintTimestamp. Cap X therefore still permits 2X phUSD per day via annihilation, unchanged.

The antimatter half is still `amount`, rate-independent (260). exchangeRate still enters only through calculateMintAmount, i.e. only the stable leg. The pre-quote at 234 makes annihilate READ the rate one step earlier, not differently: it is the same pure view with the same arguments the minter itself calls at minter:212, inside the same transaction and against the same owner-only-mutable storage, so the two readings are identical by construction and the equality check at 257 is inert with respect to exchangeRate. The one visible change is ordering: a zero-or-truncating rate now reverts PhUSDNotReceived at 235 BEFORE `_burn` (239) rather than after; since the whole transaction reverted in both versions, this is a gas/diagnostic improvement with zero economic content. The hard 1x issuance floor M-04 names is untouched — a rate cut still cannot throttle issuance below 1x, only brick it (see L-03).

deltaAssessments.direction: NEUTRAL on economics; marginal WORSENING on ordering pressure only
deltaAssessments.basis: The 2x-extraction-per-unit-of-budget leverage M-05 names is unchanged, for the same reason as M-03. One second-order ordering note, recorded but not filed: annihilate is now caller-only, so a keeper/router can no longer batch N holders' annihilations in one transaction on antimatter allowances alone; at the rolling-window roll (minter:215-217) those N holders now contend as N independent transactions for the same budget rather than one. This raises gas-auction pressure at the window boundary but changes neither the budget, the leverage, nor who ultimately wins it — the same contention already exists between annihilators and ordinary minter.mint callers, which is M-05's substance. A hook-bearing registered stablecoin would additionally allow the contention to be created atomically inside a victim's own annihilate (see ECON-009).

deltaAssessments.direction: UNCHANGED — and explicitly NOT fixed by the delta
deltaAssessments.basis: FALSE-CLOSURE HAZARD, flagged deliberately: the commit subject 'more precise mint requirement' and the new PhUSDAmountMismatch error read as a collateral-verification hardening, and they are not. calculateMintAmount (minter:243-256) is a pure function of (inputAmount, config.exchangeRate, config.decimals) and never references config.yieldStrategy or calls the yield strategy. Proving that the phUSD received equals that quote proves only that the minter performed its own arithmetic; it says nothing whatever about whether IYieldStrategy(config.yieldStrategy).deposit(stablecoin, amount, minter) (minter:229) credited anything. Antimatter's post-conditions remain exactly what M-06 described: `balanceOf(this) != stableBefore -> StableNotDeposited` (254) proves only that the stable LEFT Antimatter. This also absorbs the related surface that annihilation converts an AMM-sandwichable yield-strategy deposit into a fixed phUSD liability — the annihilator is paid `expectedForStable` regardless of YS execution quality, so any slippage on the deposit is borne entirely by phUSD backing and no actor on the path has an incentive or a parameter to limit it. That is M-06's root cause, not a new one.
deltaAssessments.action: no re-file, no re-escalation; DO NOT allow a future run to auto-propose M-06 as fixed on the strength of PhUSDAmountMismatch

deltaAssessments.basis: The root cause is unchanged: mintedForStable at 256 is still an unattributed balance delta over the window 244..256. What changed is its consequence. At 0bb82d8, phUSD arriving at Antimatter mid-call was silently forwarded to `recipient` at 261 (over-credit). At c91bc1a the same arrival fails the exact-equality check at 257 and reverts the whole annihilation. The value-leak direction of L-01 is therefore closed and a griefing/DoS direction is opened in its place. Because impact flipped but the root cause did not, this is recorded here as a delta on L-01 rather than as a new fingerprint; ECON-009 below states the griefing direction concretely and is marked as a probable duplicate of L-01 for the deduplicator to collapse.
deltaAssessments.action: keep L-01 open; update its impact narrative; see ECON-009

deltaAssessments.basis: A near-zero exchangeRate still bricks annihilation outright rather than throttling it. The only change is that the zero quote is now caught at 235 before `_burn` instead of at the old post-mint zero test, so the revert is cheaper and names PhUSDNotReceived with a clear cause. The economic property — no setting of exchangeRate can reduce annihilation output below the 1x unbacked floor, it can only stop it entirely — is untouched.

findings.severityRationale: Availability, not loss of principal: the stablecoin half is never taken on the failing path (the revert is in toStableAmount, before `_burn` at 239 and before any transfer), so nothing is stranded on-chain and no attacker profits. What is lost is the holder's ability to realise the reward leg of already-distributed antimatter against that particular stablecoin. It is recoverable by owner action (register any other stablecoin) and by holder choice (annihilate against any other registered stablecoin), and no third party controls the trigger. Not Medium because protocol function is only partially and recoverably impaired; not QA because a real, already-distributed reward entitlement becomes unrealisable for as long as the condition persists.
findings.description: Annihilation now depends on every registered stablecoin remaining willing and able to answer `decimals()`. toStableAmount makes a low-level staticcall to `IERC20Metadata.decimals` and fails closed on anything that is not exactly a 32-byte word matching the minter's registered value. Because toStableAmount is on annihilate's critical path (Antimatter.sol:230), a stablecoin that stops reporting decimals — or that never reported it in the first place — permanently disables annihilation against that stablecoin, while PhusdStableMinter.mint for the same token keeps working perfectly (the minter reads only its own config.decimals at minter:254 and never calls the token's metadata). The fault is therefore invisible on the protocol's main minting path and shows up only for antimatter holders.
findings.economicImpact: Antimatter is inert when held alone; its entire value is the `amount` of unbacked phUSD that annihilation emits for the antimatter half (Antimatter.sol:260). When the only stablecoin a holder can pair against stops answering decimals(), that reward entitlement cannot be realised at all. It is not destroyed — the antimatter is not burned on this path — but it is unrealisable until the owner registers a working alternative, and any holder who exits in the meantime does so at whatever discount the market applies to an unredeemable claim.
findings.attackScenario:
No attacker is required; this is a configuration/liveness hazard.
1. Owner registers stablecoin S (6 decimals, exchangeRate 1e18) as the only stablecoin on PhusdStableMinter.
2. Protocol distributes 10,000e18 antimatter as staking rewards over a month. Each unit is worth 1 phUSD of unbacked reward on annihilation, i.e. 10,000 phUSD of aggregate entitlement.
3. S is an upgradeable proxy. Its team ships an implementation in which `decimals()` reverts or is dropped, while `transfer`/`transferFrom` continue to work normally. (Variant with the same outcome and no upgrade at all: the owner registers an old-style token that has no `decimals()` function — annihilate then never works for S from day one, silently, because the minter supplied the decimals at registration and nothing else on the mint path ever asks the token.)
4. Every `annihilate(S, ·, ·)` reverts DecimalsUnavailable(S) at Antimatter.sol:293. `PhusdStableMinter.mint(S, ·)` is unaffected and continues to mint phUSD, so monitoring on the mint path shows the protocol healthy.
5. All 10,000e18 antimatter is unrealisable — 10,000 phUSD of distributed reward entitlement — until the owner registers a second stablecoin or migrates the minter.
findings.profitability: Not profitable to anyone. Pure availability loss to antimatter holders; no attacker gains and no protocol value is transferred out.
affectedParties: antimatter holders (staking-reward recipients) — cannot realise the reward leg
protocol — reputational/operational, must register a replacement stablecoin
externalAssumptionsRequired: The registered stablecoin's decimals() becomes unavailable (upgradeable proxy, pausable/removable metadata, self-destructed implementation) or was never present (pre-EIP-20-metadata token).
That stablecoin is the only registered one, or the affected holders hold only that stablecoin.
The owner does not promptly register an alternative stablecoin.
findings.law3Framing: Owner footgun, in scope per Law 3. A competent non-malicious owner registering a stablecoin would reasonably assume the minter's own registered `decimals` field is the authority — that is precisely why the minter carries the field — and would be surprised that annihilation additionally requires the token to self-report, and more surprised that the resulting failure is silent on the minter path and visible only to antimatter holders. Not 'a malicious owner could': the owner cannot cause this deliberately in any useful way, and third-party token behaviour is what changes.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) treat an unavailable decimals() as 'no independent confirmation available' and fall back to the registered value rather than reverting, keeping the hard revert only for a decimals() that answers and DISAGREES (which is the actual misconfiguration M-01 aimed at); or (b) do the cross-check once, at owner-registration/acceptance time on Antimatter's side, and cache it, so a later change in token behaviour cannot brick already-distributed rewards; or (c) accept as-is and document the operational requirement that at least two independently-implemented stablecoins are registered at all times, plus a monitor that calls toStableAmount(S, 1e18) per registered S.
findings.mightBeIntentional: Partly. The NatSpec at 288-296 explicitly chooses fail-closed ('A disagreement is a configuration fault for a human to resolve, so it fails closed rather than preferring either side's value') and even notes 'Off-chain callers using this as a quote helper therefore depend on `stable` being responsive.' The DISAGREEMENT case is clearly intentional and correct. What is not evidenced as a considered trade-off is the UNAVAILABLE case being treated identically to the disagreement case, nor the asymmetry that leaves the minter path working while the annihilate path bricks.

findings.type: griefing / atomic-DoS via unattributed balance delta
findings.severityRationale: Griefing only, no profit and no principal loss: the victim loses gas on a reverted transaction and the griefer spends 1 wei of phUSD plus gas per attempt. Gated behind an owner registration choice (a callback-bearing stablecoin), which no realistic registered stable (USDC/USDT/DAI-class) satisfies. Low, and likely collapsible into L-01.
findings.description: The new exact-equality post-check compares an unattributed balance delta against a quote. `mintedForStable` (256) is the change in Antimatter's phUSD balance across the window 244..256, and `expectedForStable` (234) is what the minter's arithmetic promises. Any phUSD that reaches Antimatter from any other source inside that window makes the two disagree and reverts the whole annihilation with PhUSDAmountMismatch. At 0bb82d8 the identical donation was silently forwarded to `recipient` (over-credit, L-01); the delta converts that value-leak into a revert, which is the right trade for value but creates a new atomic griefing surface for any actor that can obtain execution during the window.
findings.codeSnippet:
uint256 mintedForStable = _phUSD.balanceOf(address(this)) - phUSDBefore;
if (mintedForStable != expectedForStable) revert PhUSDAmountMismatch(expectedForStable, mintedForStable);
findings.possibleDuplicateOf: L-01 / ad4b779566291190 (same root cause — unattributed balance delta at 256 — opposite impact). Deduplicator: collapse into L-01 if L-01's narrative is updated per deltaAssessments.L-01; keep separate only if the ledger prefers impact-keyed entries.
findings.economicImpact: Denial of annihilation for as long as the griefer keeps paying. No value moves: the burn at 239 is unwound by the revert, so the victim's antimatter and stablecoin are intact.
findings.attackScenario:
Requires a registered stablecoin H that grants execution to a third party during transferFrom (ERC777-style callback, or any hook-bearing token).
1. Owner registers H (18 decimals, exchangeRate 1e18). Attacker holds 1 wei of phUSD.
2. Victim calls annihilate(H, victim, 100e18). expectedForStable = 100e18 is fixed at line 234; phUSDBefore is captured at 244.
3. During safeTransferFrom(H) at 246, H's hook gives the attacker execution. The attacker transfers 1 wei of phUSD to Antimatter. (nonReentrant at 221 blocks re-entering annihilate, but nothing blocks a plain phUSD transfer INTO Antimatter.)
4. At 256, mintedForStable = 100e18 + 1. At 257 it != expectedForStable, so PhUSDAmountMismatch(100e18, 100e18+1) reverts the transaction.
5. Cost to attacker: 1 wei phUSD (refunded by the revert of the outer tx? no — the attacker's own transfer is unwound too, so the true cost is only the gas the victim's transaction pays, which the victim bears). Net: the attacker griefs for free from within the victim's own gas budget, repeatably, for every annihilation against H.
Variant with the same precondition and the same outcome: instead of donating phUSD, the hook calls PhusdStableMinter.mint(H, x) directly to consume the remaining maxMintPerDay budget, so the outer minter.mint at 251 reverts 'Daily mint limit exceeded'. That variant is the atomic form of the contention M-05 already describes.
findings.profitability: Not profitable — pure griefing. Becomes economically motivated only for an actor with an external short position in antimatter or an interest in suppressing phUSD issuance; state that assumption explicitly rather than assuming it.
affectedParties: annihilators using the affected stablecoin (gas loss, denied access)
antimatter holders (cannot realise rewards against that stablecoin)
externalAssumptionsRequired: The owner has registered a stablecoin that grants execution to a third party during transfer/transferFrom (ERC777 or other hook-bearing token). No mainstream stablecoin in the plausible registration set does this.
The attacker can position a contract to receive that callback (trivial once the precondition holds — the mock test/mocks/ReentrantStable.sol already demonstrates hook execution against annihilate).
For the cap variant: maxMintPerDay is non-zero for that stablecoin.
findings.law3Framing: Owner footgun. Registering a callback-bearing token is the enabling decision, and its consequence here (a stranger can abort other users' annihilations from inside their own transactions) is not obvious from the registration API. The reentrancy guard at 221 and the ReentrantStable mock may reasonably read as having settled the hook-token question; they settle re-entry, not third-party donation.
findings.recommendation: Either accept the equality check as a deliberate strict tripwire and document that hook-bearing stablecoins must never be registered, or make the check one-sided — `if (mintedForStable < expectedForStable) revert PhUSDAmountMismatch(...)` — which preserves the short-mint detection the commit was aiming at while making a donation harmless again (and, unlike the pre-delta behaviour, the surplus would still need explicit handling to avoid re-opening L-01's over-credit).
findings.mightBeIntentional: The strict equality is clearly deliberate ('a short mint cannot pass unnoticed', 233-234). Whether the choice of equality over a `<` bound was weighed against the donation-griefing consequence is not evidenced anywhere in the source or CLAUDE.md.

answersToTaskQuestions.q1_exactEqualityVsM03M04M05: Economically INERT on all three, in both directions. M-04: the quote at 234 and the minter's own quote at 212 are the same pure view, same arguments, same transaction, over storage only the owner can mutate — they are identical by construction, so the check can never fire on an exchangeRate ground and cannot re-price either leg. M-03/M-05: the daily cap is a revert (minter:221), never a haircut, so a cap event aborts inside minter.mint at Antimatter.sol:251 and never reaches the check at 257; and calculateMintAmount cannot encode the cap because it reads only exchangeRate and decimals (minter:248-255). The check's real domain is therefore narrow: it fires only if (a) phUSD reaches Antimatter mid-call from elsewhere (ECON-009 / L-01) or (b) the minter or phUSD deviates from this code — i.e. it is a tripwire against a swapped, upgraded or misbehaving minter, not against normal operation. No new distinct root cause is created on the M-03/M-04/M-05 axis.
answersToTaskQuestions.q2_decimalsStaticcallAvailability: Filed as ECON-008 (Low). Stranded reward-antimatter is AVAILABILITY, not value loss, on three independent grounds: the revert happens in toStableAmount before `_burn` (239) so nothing is consumed or stranded on-chain; `stable` is a free parameter of annihilate so a holder can pair against any other registered stablecoin; and the owner can register a replacement at will. It degrades to real economic loss only in the compound case where the bricking token is the sole registered stablecoin AND the owner does not replace it — which is why Low rather than QA. Severity would rise to Medium only if annihilate could be shown to consume the antimatter before the decimals check, which it cannot (the check is at 292, reached from 230, which precedes 239).
answersToTaskQuestions.q3_decimalsCrossCheckArbitrageOrOrdering: NO new arbitrage and NO new ordering incentive. The cross-check is a pure view, deterministic within a block, and its only possible effect is to make annihilate revert — it can never make annihilate produce a different quantity, because the arithmetic at 296-299 uses the REGISTERED `decimals`, not the value read at 292. A token that reports inconsistent decimals across calls therefore gains nothing: the single reading is a gate, not an input, and both Antimatter (296) and the minter (254) scale by the same registered field regardless. The only ordering-adjacent effect is a race with owner reconfiguration: re-registering a stablecoin at different decimals (minter:111) makes in-flight annihilate transactions revert DecimalsMismatch — fail-closed, no profit either side.
answersToTaskQuestions.q4_callerOnlyEconomicDependency: NO economic flow the protocol depends on is lost. Delegation of the OUTPUT survives intact: `recipient` is still a free parameter (223, 260, 261), so a keeper, router or zap can annihilate on a user's behalf by taking custody of both legs for the span of one transaction — pull the user's antimatter via ERC20 transferFrom into the router, pull the stablecoin, approve Antimatter, call annihilate(stable, user, amount) — and the user receives all 2x phUSD directly. Batching also survives: one router transaction can loop over N users this way. The single flow that is now impossible is annihilating from a holder who has APPROVED antimatter but not transferred it, i.e. gasless/meta-transaction annihilation on allowance alone — which is precisely the H-01 vector, so its removal is the fix, not a casualty. Grounded in economic need rather than existing code, as instructed: no staking, reward, migration or router contract anywhere in lib/ or src/ calls annihilate (only test/ and test/mocks/ReentrantStable.sol), so there is no incumbent integration to break; and the reward's realisation path (holder supplies their own stable, receives 2x phUSD) has no structural reason to require a third-party burner. Residual, non-economic and QA-level at most: the Annihilated event's indexed field is now `annihilator` = msg.sender, so under a router pattern it names the router rather than the beneficiary; any off-chain accounting keyed on the old `from` field would attribute the burn to the intermediary. `recipient` remains the correct attribution key.
answersToTaskQuestions.q5_mevOrderingOnAnnihilate: No NEW MEV is introduced by the delta. The standing mechanic is unchanged and is intended: annihilation emits `amount` phUSD against no incoming value, so whenever antimatter trades on any secondary market at price P < 1 phUSD, buying antimatter at P and annihilating is risk-free profit of amount*(1-P) per unit (concrete: buy 1,000e18 AM at 0.90 phUSD = 900 phUSD, supply 1,000e6 USDC at exchangeRate 1e18, receive 1,000e18 + 1,000e18 = 2,000e18 phUSD for 900 phUSD + 1,000 USDC in, net +100 phUSD). This pins antimatter's market price to ~1 phUSD minus friction and is the M-02 mechanism the owner has accepted; it is not re-filed. The delta changes only WHO must hold the stablecoin leg during that trade (the arbitrageur, rather than a holder they hold an allowance over), which is a neutral-to-positive change in ordering terms because it removes the ability to sequence an annihilation against a passive holder's balance. The remaining ordering surfaces are pre-existing and already-triaged: contention for maxMintPerDay at the window roll (M-05, worsened only marginally by the loss of batching — see deltaAssessments.M-05), and sandwich exposure on the yield-strategy deposit whose loss lands on phUSD backing rather than on the annihilator (M-06). No sandwich of annihilate itself is possible: it quotes and settles atomically with no AMM on Antimatter's own path and no slippage parameter to exploit.

explicitlyNotFiled.reason: M-02, wont-fix, owner rationale accepted. Also covered by the recorded principle that value already generated by prior staked capital and re-issued as reward is a distribution decision, not a value leak.

explicitlyNotFiled.reason: Atomic variant of M-05 (wont-fix) with the same root cause and the same owner-registration precondition as ECON-009; recorded inside ECON-009's attackScenario rather than minting a third overlapping fingerprint.

explicitlyNotFiled.reason: M-06, wont-fix. calculateMintAmount is YS-blind by construction; this is that finding's substance, not a new one.

explicitlyNotFiled.reason: Fee-on-transfer tokens are a C4 known-invalid category, and phUSD is first-party FlaxToken v2 with no fee.

explicitlyNotFiled.candidate: Rounding/precision on the decimals rescale and on calculateMintAmount's /1e18 truncation.
explicitlyNotFiled.reason: Tier-1 territory (verified in the profile: AmountNotRepresentable at 299 enforces exact representability, and Antimatter compares two truncations of the identical expression so truncation cannot itself cause divergence). No cross-contract composition of rounding directions exists on this path: there is exactly one division on the value path and both consumers of it read the same result.

roundingChecklistResult.applicable: partially — annihilate is a conversion, not a share/asset vault operation; there is no share price, no round-trip and no redeem leg.
roundingChecklistResult.userReceives: amount (exact, no division) + calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount) (floor division by 1e18 at minter:255 — rounds DOWN, in the protocol's favour). Correct direction.
roundingChecklistResult.userPays: stableAmount = amount / 10**(18-decimals), guarded by `stableAmount * scale != amount -> AmountNotRepresentable` (Antimatter.sol:298-299), so the division is exact and never rounds in the user's favour. Correct — no floor-in-the-user's-favour is reachable.
roundingChecklistResult.roundTrip: There is no reverse operation. phUSD cannot be converted back to antimatter and the stablecoin half is not redeemable through Antimatter, so no composed round-trip exists to leak on. The economically asymmetric leg is the unbacked `amount` mint, which is a deliberate reward emission (M-02), not a rounding artefact.
roundingChecklistResult.verdict: No rounding-direction defect. Every division on the path either rounds down on what the user receives or is proven exact.

parkedForVisibleFollowUp.detail: PhUSDAmountMismatch must not be accepted as evidence that the yield-strategy crediting is verified. Any future run proposing M-06 (ac6de2faade9adcd) as fixed on the strength of the equality check should be rejected; a genuine fix requires observing the YS position, which nothing on this path does.

L-01's ledger narrative currently describes an over-credit. Post-delta the same root cause produces a revert instead. The entry should be re-worded rather than closed — closing it would lose the surviving unattributed-delta root cause.

The decimals cross-check protects only Antimatter's path. A decimals misregistration still mis-scales silently for every direct PhusdStableMinter.mint caller. Out of first-party scope (minter lives under antimatter's lib/), parked here so it is not lost if the minter is ever brought in scope.

If ECON-008 is accepted rather than fixed, the protocol acquires an undocumented operational invariant: at least two registered stablecoins with independent metadata implementations, plus liveness monitoring on toStableAmount per registered stable. That invariant exists nowhere in CLAUDE.md or the NatSpec today.

assumptionsMade: PhusdStableMinter at lib/phUSD-stable-minter (d6ed1156) is the version that will be deployed; the cap-is-a-revert and quote-purity conclusions are read from minter:203-256 at that pin.

Antimatter is distributed as a staking reward to holders who also hold, or can acquire, one of the registered stablecoins. If any material share of antimatter is distributed to addresses that cannot supply a stablecoin, ECON-008's impact rises and the caller-only change (q4) would deserve re-examination.
No registered stablecoin grants execution to third parties during transfer/transferFrom. ECON-009 is conditional on this assumption being violated by a future registration.
The `exchangeRate` for registered stablecoins is 1e18 (1:1) in the intended configuration; the numeric scenarios above use that rate.

No deployment script or reward distributor for antimatter exists in the repository at c91bc1a, so the actual registered-stablecoin set at deployment is unknown; ECON-008's 'sole registered stablecoin' precondition could not be confirmed or excluded from source.
